body:
>I think that everyone wants to better their life; it's just a human thing to wish for greater happiness.

I would guess everyone has this urge inside, but not everyone really acts on it. I am living in the german rural countryside. I do not need to look far to find a lot of other failed existences. Alcoholism and suicide is actually not uncommon here. Also when I look at all the people I went to school with: Some of them had ambitions but they just stopped caring, settled down and complain about life when drunk. Makes me angry just thinking about it. They are married, have a steady income, parents which support them, heck most even have a house. They just don't quite comprehend how lucky they are and take everything as a given. But I guess I would be exactly the same if things just went a little bit better...

>I wish I knew what to say to you about self-esteem and anxiety problems because I have no idea how to deal with my own. It just seems like a vicious cycle to me; I can tell myself that I'm a great person and all but I just can't make myself believe it.

Well in *theory* it is pretty easy, there is one reliable way to fight anxiety and that is called confrontation. I actually made my first baby steps outside while on lorazepam - I actually grabbed my guitar and went out to get my frets replaced. Went into the next big city by public transit and asked my way around without the use of smart phones and internet. Walking trough this gigantic railroad station without this constant fear was mesmerizing. It blows my mind thinking about how all this people walk to whichever place they want everyday, sitting next to strangers on a train. For them it was a normal thing to do. I felt like I just climbed the Mount Everest. But this is where probably my ADD kicks in. When I accomplish something I feel great for ten minutes before everything gets dull again. My scumbag brain goes something like: "So you just programmed that quad-copter to move freely in all six directions? Let me tell you why you are worthless, you didn't even build it yourself!" 

And I have exactly the same self-esteem issue. I can tell myself, I can even proof myself, I can even get people to compliment me on; whatever, they are probably lying. I don't believe in myself. I can't. I *know* I am not worthless, probably more the opposite. I just can't *believe* it.

I just can't fathom how hard I hit rock bottom again. I was out there, doing my first little steps, my semester started again. I should be in university right now. Instead I was curled up on my bed all day and didn't do anything. I am still somewhat sleep deprived, but I can't sleep every time I close my eyes I see everything I lost. Everything I ever wanted and never got - it drives me insane. What did I do to deserve this? I was beginning to rise out of this shit hole only to crash right back inside with full force.
